When catch-up phase is in progress and a parallel db write is executed it is possible that the write is lost as it is not neither caught by snapshot nor by stremaing pahse as it can get filtered.

To reproduce check {{io.debezium.connector.postgresql.PostgresConnectorIT.shouldResumeStreamingFromSlotPositionForCustomSnapshotWal2Json()}} and execute it for decoderbufs. The LSN of the parallel write gets filtered due to LSN comparison. If the LSN filtering is disabled in the code the record gets in.

This is problem only for custom snapshotters with {{shouldStreamEventsStartingFromSnapshot()}} set to {{false}}.

The Oracle connector requires installation of the Oracle Instant Client. The Instant Client library has libaio as a dependency. The connector container (debezium/connect:1.2) doesn't have libaio installed, and since it doesn't support yum or sudo, we can't install it. 

The request is to rebuild the debezium connector with libaio so it will be compatible with Oracle Instant Client.

I actually found the root cause of the bug:

In [this line|https://github.com/debezium/debezium/blob/3ada04b522370e96ce8cfef30c7aedc725828fe2/debezium-core/src/main/java/io/debezium/transforms/ExtractNewRecordState.java#L237]:
{code:java}
updatedValue.put(field.name(), value.get(field)); {code}
The Struct [get method|https://github.com/a0x8o/kafka/blob/7fcbe62fd2d573cd6e860bad084a61d959fe6729/connect/api/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/connect/data/Struct.java#L85] replaces the null value with the field's default value.

To fix this undesired behavior the [getWithoutDefault|https://github.com/a0x8o/kafka/blob/7fcbe62fd2d573cd6e860bad084a61d959fe6729/connect/api/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/connect/data/Struct.java#L98] method should be used instead:
{code:java}
updatedValue.put(field.name(), value.getWithoutDefault(field.name())); {code}
There are a few more potential "buggy" lines in the SMT's code which can easily be fixed in the same way..

The issue seems to be that we are passing what is not json to a json parser. This stems from when we get the collection value json and and parse out the three fields we are looking for ({{{}id{}}},{{{} type{}}},{{{} data{}}}) using {{{}Document.parse{}}}. However for the {{data}} value when calling an "execute-snapshot" signal the {{data}} contains a string of json. This causes issues later on as we are looping though the fields and calling {{.toString()}} as the string representation of \{{Document}} is not json. 

[https://github.com/debezium/debezium/blob/main/debezium-connector-mongodb/src/main/java/io/debezium/connector/mongodb/MongoDbConnectorConfig.java#L836]

 Instead for {{{}Object'{}}}s that are of type {{Document}} we should be calling the {{.toJson()}} to format the string correctly because later on we are expecting to parse json where the error is thrown:

[https://github.com/debezium/debezium/blob/main/debezium-core/src/main/java/io/debezium/pipeline/signal/Signal.java#L134]

 When table schema changes, an incremental snapshot is triggered by inserting a row into the signal table. This is done right after the schema change, so that no new change events with the new schema have been received yet.

 Incremental snapshot recognises the updated schema and completes without errors.

 Incremental snapshot does not recognise the updated schema and fails, both for adding and removing a column. The flush strategy was reworked as a part of DBZ-2552.  A regression was introduced that causes the connector to insert multiple rows into the flush table under specific conditions which are unintended.

The connector makes several calls to {{OracleConnectorConfig#getDatabaseHistory}} over its streaming iteration which leads to multiple executors being created and discarded as well as lots of unnecessary logging.  

Ideally these site usages should be replaced with calls to {{OracleDatabaseSchema}} to get whatever history context values are needed by delegating to the already created and configured {{DatabaseHistory}} implementation.

The builds are failing on postgis installation.

This is a follow up to DBZ-4049. A pom was extended to override MySQL driver version that were pulled from Quarkus.

We need to make sure there is not the same problem with other drivers.
Also when Postgres was attempted to fix there was an issue with postgres tests running as part of {{debezium-sever}} workflow hanging.

The expectation was that issuing a transaction commit causes the LGWR buffer to flush, but this is only applicable to the current transaction and not other transactions that may be in progress at the time.  The processing logic was taking the {{endScn}} as the starting boundary for subsequent mining sessions and this could lead to events being lost.

For example, lets take a mining session from [1000, 1099].  If events near the end of the boundary are still in the LGWR buffer and aren't flushed to the redo logs, then the mining session would only get a subset of the records.  The processor returned the {{endScn}} which is 1099 in this case as the starting point for the next iteration but if events 1090 through 1099 were still in the LGWR buffer, they would be skipped and not emitted. 

The solution is by default, we cannot take the {{endScn}} value as an absolute breakpoint in the mining iterations but instead need to compare it to the last processed Scn we got from the result-set.  If the last processed Scn is before the {{endScn}} value, then we need to use the {{lastProcessedScn}} as the starting point for the next iteration instead.
